title: Legacy CRM Configuration Architecture — Admin Console Hub, Metadata Cache Lifecycle, and Profile-Based Settings
summary: The configuration architecture for a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the centralized admin console as the tile-based configuration hub, the metadata cache generation and synchronization lifecycle that propagates configuration changes to mobile devices, and the profile-based settings model that controls feature behavior per user segment.

findings.admin_console_configuration_hub: The Admin Console serves as the centralized configuration surface for all platform features. Each functional domain (CLM, Products, Call Administration, Orders, Meetings, Territories, Mobile, Monitoring, and others) is represented as a navigable tile. Within each tile, configuration is organized into sub-tabs — for example, the CLM tile contains Sequences, Presentations, and Settings tabs. Configuration changes made through the Admin Console do not take effect on mobile devices immediately. Instead, they require a metadata cache generation step followed by a synchronization cycle to propagate changes to field devices.
findings.metadata_cache_generation_and_sync: Every configuration change follows a three-phase propagation model: (1) Admin makes the change through the Admin Console or platform setup. (2) Admin triggers a metadata cache generation, which compiles all current configuration state into a distributable metadata package. (3) Mobile devices download the updated metadata package during their next synchronization cycle. This architecture means configuration changes are never real-time on mobile — there is always a latency window between configuration and field availability. The cache generation step is a deliberate design choice that allows administrators to batch multiple changes before pushing them to the field, preventing partial configurations from reaching devices.
findings.profile_based_settings_model: Feature behavior is controlled at the user profile level through a settings matrix. The CLM Settings page, for example, exposes per-profile toggle controls for capabilities like Training Mode (disables time tracking for slide views), Presentation Lockdown (prevents field modification of presentation sequences), Geolocation Tracking (captures GPS coordinates during presentations), and Favorite Presentations (enables local bookmarking of frequently-used content). This profile-scoping model allows different user populations (field representatives, district managers, medical science liaisons, home office users) to have different feature configurations without requiring separate application builds or deployments.
findings.permission_gated_feature_activation: Features are activated through a layered permission model combining profile settings, permission sets, and custom permissions. For example, enabling the Send-by-Email capability for CLM presentations requires both a specific permission (Enable Sending CLM by Email) and the feature configuration in CLM Settings. Custom presentations require a dedicated permission (Manage Custom CLM Presentation on Mobile) plus the creation of a specific topic record. This dual-gate pattern — permission plus configuration — is repeated across most platform features, ensuring that both access control and feature behavior are independently manageable.

title: Legacy CRM Configuration Domains — CLM Presentation Management, Product Hierarchy, Territory Alignment, and Call Administration
summary: The major configuration domains within a legacy life sciences CRM, covering CLM presentation lifecycle management (upload, sequencing, availability, email distribution), product hierarchy and type classification, territory-based product alignment with five alignment states, and the administrative controls governing field call execution.

findings.clm_presentation_lifecycle: CLM presentations follow a configured lifecycle: upload (ZIP or PDF to the platform), sequence assembly (ordering individual slides into recommended interaction flows with mandatory flags and reporting field assignments), availability control (active flag plus date-range windowing), and territory alignment (hierarchical parent-child distribution with an allow-unaligned toggle). Presentations support product-level restriction rules that control which content is available based on the products aligned to a representative's territory. Each presentation has configurable player behavior including gesture options, zoom controls (pinch and double-tap), and content rating metadata. The reporting field set on presentations enables administrators to define which metadata fields appear in engagement analytics.
findings.product_hierarchy_and_type_system: Products are organized in a multi-level hierarchy with nine distinct product types: Detail (promotional messaging), Brand (product brand grouping), Market (market-level grouping), Sample (physical product samples), Item (inventory items), Bundle (grouped items for distribution), Order Item (orderable products), Kit Item (components within order items), and Rx Product (prescription products). Parent-child relationships follow specific rules — Detail, Brand, and Market types can parent Sample, Item, and Bundle types, while Brand can also parent Order Items, and Kit Items can only be children of Order Items. This type system governs which operations are available on each product (sampling, ordering, messaging, territory alignment) and how products roll up in reporting hierarchies.
findings.territory_product_alignment: Product-to-territory alignment uses a five-state model: Not Aligned (product not available in territory), Directly Aligned (explicitly assigned), Excluded (explicitly removed from a territory that would otherwise inherit it), Parent-Aligned (inherited from a parent territory), and Aligned-with-Children (aligned at this level and propagated downward). Alignment can be managed individually through the Admin Console or in bulk via CSV import using a territory-product alignment rule entity. Exclusion and inclusion rules operate only at bottom-level territories, providing granular control over which products field representatives can access. Product Territory Allocations add quantity limits scoped to plan cycles with per-call maximum validation, controlling how many units of each product a representative can distribute.
findings.call_administration_and_field_controls: Call administration configuration governs the rules and behavior of field visits. Product messaging is configured per product (Brand and Detail types only) with priority ordering, display text, custom reaction options (semicolon-separated values), and date-range validation that prevents messages from being active outside their parent product's date range. Message grouping organizes related messages into ordered groups through designated fields and a global enable toggle. Sample lot management controls lot number assignment, expiration date tracking, and active status — lots are allocated to individual users through sample lot allocation records. The administration layer also controls call-level features like signature capture requirements, document ID verification alternatives, and post-call workflow routing.

title: Legacy CRM Deep Configuration Patterns — Territory Distribution, Bulk Operations, Content Distribution Controls, and Feature Toggle Architecture
summary: The advanced configuration patterns in a legacy life sciences CRM, covering the territory-based content and product distribution model, bulk operation capabilities for scale administration, content distribution controls (email sending, custom presentations, favorites), and the layered feature toggle architecture that governs platform behavior.

findings.territory_distribution_model: Territory hierarchy is the primary distribution mechanism for both content and products. CLM presentations and products are aligned at territory nodes, with inheritance flowing downward through the hierarchy. Administrators can break inheritance at any level through exclusion rules (removing an item from a child territory that would otherwise inherit it) or inclusion rules (adding an item to a specific bottom-level territory independent of parent alignment). This model means that a single alignment action at a high-level territory can distribute content or products to hundreds of field representatives, while exclusions provide the escape valve for regional or regulatory differences. The allow-unaligned toggle on presentations provides an override that makes content available regardless of territory alignment — useful for corporate communications or training content that should reach all users.
findings.bulk_operation_capabilities: Scale administration is supported through bulk operations across multiple configuration domains. Presentations support bulk upload (multiple ZIP files in a single operation), bulk update (modifying metadata across multiple presentations simultaneously), and bulk edit (changing sequence configurations in batch). Product-to-territory alignment supports CSV-based bulk import through alignment rule entities. These bulk capabilities are essential for organizations managing thousands of products across hundreds of territories — individual record management would be impractical at this scale. Bulk operations follow the same metadata cache generation requirement as individual changes, allowing administrators to batch all bulk modifications before a single cache generation push.
findings.content_distribution_controls: Three specialized distribution channels extend CLM content beyond in-person presentation: (1) Send-by-Email allows representatives to email presentation content to healthcare providers, with configurable attachment behavior — files under a size threshold (approximately 3MB) are auto-attached, while larger files are sent as links. Required attachments are designated through a naming prefix convention. The feature requires both a permission grant and support for the platform's file entity type for content storage and delivery. (2) Custom Presentations allow representatives to create their own HTML-only presentations for personal use, with administrator-created content remaining read-only. Custom content requires a dedicated topic record and permission assignment. (3) Favorite Presentations enable local bookmarking on the device for quick access during calls — stored locally and lost on logout, requiring no server-side configuration beyond permission enablement.
findings.feature_toggle_architecture: The platform uses a four-layer feature toggle architecture: (1) Organization-level settings control platform-wide feature availability. (2) Profile-level settings enable or disable features for user segments — the primary configuration surface for most features. (3) Permission sets grant the access rights needed to use enabled features — features can be profile-enabled but permission-blocked, creating a deliberate separation between feature availability and access authorization. (4) Custom permissions provide granular sub-feature control within a broader feature area. This layered model means that activating a feature for a user population requires coordinating changes across multiple layers. The configuration guide documents the specific combination of settings, permissions, and custom permissions required for each feature, as the interaction between layers is not always intuitive from the individual setting descriptions alone.
